title: A binary state form flips at a predeclared threshold
summary: A threshold model assigns a binary state marker to whether a measured property is below or above one fixed threshold, rather than treating the marker as an ordinal quantity or free quality modifier.

design.unit: records with a comparable measured property and a binary state form
design.prediction: After calibrating the threshold on a designated development set, all held values on the same scale below it receive one state and all above it the other, with no dependence on record position.
design.countermodel: The proposed rule may be an analyst projection: the same observations could arise from a context-conditioned lexical or editorial convention without the proposed semantic operator.
design.falsifier: A held value on the same scale crosses the threshold but retains the old state, or equal-side values split by position with no scale change.
design.principal_risk: A shared physical scale and independent measurements are unknown; no threshold is asserted. Near quantity/grade cards, but its falsifier is a fixed decision boundary rather than conservation, ordinal counting, or degree insertion.
